description_en: A well preserved stone fountain from circa 14th-15th century.The fountain is located on the side of the track connecting Kālikā Bājār to Samālgāũ.The fountain is constituted of a central wall facing west and framed on each side by a small platform. The central wall and platforms are carved with plinths and projections (skt.bhadra), similar to the ones onśikharatemple facades. Two spouts in the upper section are connected to a stone channel visible on top of the fountain. The spouts are shaped with the head of amakara, similar to the ones on medieval fountains (hiti) in the Kathmandu Valley.Similar fountains, locally referred to asmugrāhā, are found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019). This monument can be roughly dated to the 14th-15th century, a period corresponding to the rise of the Rāskoṭī dynasty (14th-16th century).This is one of the best preserved fountains in this part of the Karnali basin.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019.
